events.title: ECMAScript 3 standard adopted (ECMA-262 3rd edition)
events.summary: Ecma adopted ECMA-262 3rd edition in December 1999 — adding regex, try/catch, and better string handling to JavaScript.
events.about: ES3 is the JavaScript dialect the web ran on for a decade — the baseline every browser implemented before ES5 and ES2015. It added regular expressions, exceptions, and tighter error rules that made complex client-side code possible. Most pre-2015 tutorials and libraries assumed ES3 semantics.

narrative.whyChosen: ES3 was the stable JavaScript most of the web learned and deployed for ten years.
narrative.whyImportant: It added the error-handling and regex features dynamic web apps needed without breaking existing pages.
narrative.problemSolved: Early JavaScript lacked robust string matching and exception handling for growing client-side complexity.
